html:
The Jumano were one people, or several, of west Texas, New Mexico and northern Mexico, met by Spanish explorers from 1581. Some lived in farming towns at La Junta de los Ríos, where the Conchos River joins the Rio Grande; others were bison hunters and traders who travelled widely across the southern Plains.

They are best known as go-betweens, linking the Pueblos of New Mexico, the Caddo of east Texas and the Spanish settlements. In 1629 a Jumano party asked for missionaries, saying a "lady in blue" had preached to them; this was tied to the Spanish nun María de Ágreda, who claimed to have visited them in visions. From the late 1600s the Apache took over the southern Plains, and the Jumano faded, merging with the Apache, Comanche and others. Who exactly they were is still debated.
